launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-matrix
_doc_vendored_engine: CI does NOT run the engine source in 1_cicd/src/scripts — it runs the VENDORED COPY at ./build.sh, from this directory. This key DECLARES that copy relationship so the workflow generator can enforce byte-identity (cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, step 'verify engine ↔ vendored build.sh parity') and go red on drift. Editing the engine alone used to change nothing at ship time, silently — which is how the ABI gate and the GHCR auto-delete gate came to exist only in the file nobody executes. Re-sync with: cp 1_cicd/src/scripts/<engine> ./build.sh

matrix._alt_id_doc: Real installed package of the resigned STOCK Element X APK (io.element.android.x, extracted from the fdroid release manifest). Detection + install use this, never app_id.
matrix._blocked_on_history: Was 'matrix-chat-bridge-stack-ship' (continuwuity + mautrix-whatsapp + element stack). Unblocked 2026-07-09 to publish the standalone GHCR APK for the Constellation AppStore — the resigned upstream Element X APK installs independent of the homeserver; the app is non-functional until the Matrix backend stack is deployed.
matrix.comment: Element X Android (Kotlin + Rust matrix-sdk FFI). Exporter reads via the Rust-SDK Kotlin BINDINGS, never raw store files. Push via UnifiedPush with our ntfy (rss.diegonmarcos.com) as distributor — Element X supports it natively.

upstream_apk._doc: Pinned UPSTREAM RELEASE APK — bundle fallback (owner directive 2026-06-12: ALL apps ship inside the hub NOW). bundle-forks embeds this sha256-verified APK whenever our own fork image isn't on GHCR yet; the patched fork replaces it the moment its CI lands. resign=true → the engine zipalign+apksigner's it with the constellation key (Mattermost publishes unsigned APKs — unsigned can't install; our key also makes it IPC-compatible). NOTE: blocked_on gates OUR fork build (homeserver work), not stock-client bundling — Element X is a generic Matrix client.

abi_variants._doc: Per-ABI upstream assets. bundle-forks picks abi_variants[$COMMS_BUNDLE_ABI] when set (default arm64-v8a uses the top-level url/sha256). x86_64 = Waydroid debug builds.

x86_64._doc_sha256: Re-pinned 2026-08-20. element-hq REPLACED this release asset in place: the URL now serves a2b626ec... where the pin said 33f8baf3..., and every ship-cloud-matrix run since 2026-08-18 died on the mismatch. Re-pinned only after checking provenance, not to make CI pass: the arm64-v8a asset from the SAME tag still matches its pin byte-for-byte (so the release was not wholesale re-uploaded); the new file carries the same upstream git revision 337528bce386f1731701f9ac2d0cbc190e244e02 and versionName 26.06.2 as that known-good arm64 APK; and both are signed by the same certificate, New Vector Ltd./element.io, SHA-256 6A:2F:DC:31:48:04:9C:E0:D5:C6:E8:50:10:72:3B:83:FB:20:7D:20:C7:47:7F:5C:22:AC:53:C8:77:E9:2D:47. If a future mismatch does NOT satisfy all four checks, do not re-pin - investigate.

matrix._doc_vendored: Vendored in-repo 2026-08-30: the full Element X Android source lives at this repo's root, patched and committed, so nothing is cloned at build time. materialize-fork takes the vendored path (tracker_dir exists and holds no .git), patches/ is historical record only. To move to a newer upstream tag, bump pinned_tag, delete the vendored tree and let the clone+patch path re-vendor it.

build._doc: Module `app`, flavor `fdroid` (dimension `store`) - the Google-free flavor, matching the release asset upstream_apk used to pin. The Rust matrix-sdk is consumed as a PREBUILT maven artifact (org.matrix.rustcomponents:sdk-android, gradle/libs.versions.toml), so this is a plain gradle build with no Rust toolchain and no cargo/NDK cross-compilation step.
build._doc_signing: app/build.gradle.kts's own 'release' buildType hardcodes signingConfig = signingConfigs.debug (never reads keystore.properties), and that debug signingConfig points at a repo-local ./signature/debug.keystore that *.keystore's repo-wide .gitignore keeps out of the vendored tree — so it never exists on a fresh checkout. signing=debug_keystore generates the STANDARD, well-known, non-secret Android debug keystore (androiddebugkey/android, matches signingConfigs.debug exactly) at keystore_dest so the fdroid-release build has something to sign with at all. Because the resulting APK is therefore only debug-signed, resign_unsigned strips that and re-signs with the ONE shared constellation key afterward — same as every other fork's real release artifact.

matrix._doc_rebrand: Rebranded in the vendored tree (patches/0001, historical record): BuildTimeConfig.APPLICATION_ID is now app_id and APPLICATION_NAME is 'Cloud Matrix', so the from-source build ships under our identity rather than upstream's. alt_id stays: Fleet.installedId checks app_id FIRST and falls back to alt_id, which is what still detects a previously installed resigned STOCK build so it can be replaced. Launcher artwork in appicon/element/ is NOT yet replaced - see NOTICE.md.

modules._doc: Shared modules settings.gradle.kts includes BY REFERENCE. Declared so the ship workflow watches them and the publish gate hashes them: a change to any of them must rebuild Cloud Matrix, not ride along unshipped. settings.gradle.kts still names them as literals (upstream's file, not a loop over this map).

libs:location-client._doc: #1770 the one client of location: reads Cloud Nav's last fix over the fleet IPC door, never triggers a fix.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleet-data-client._doc: #1566 libs:core and libs:fleetconfig-model read the fleet-config manifest through this client (a fleet-private served dataset); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

gh_release._doc: Rolling GH release 'latest' (shared across the ea_cloud-* apps; each contributes a distinctly-named APK asset), overwritten every main push so https://github.com/diegonmarcos/cloudy-u-android/releases/latest/download/cloud-comms-matrix.apk stays stable. Published by `build.sh gh-release-fork matrix` (ship-cloud-matrix.yml), which uploads dist/cloud-comms-matrix.apk with --clobber. Consumed by aa_cloud-superapp ui.external_apps[cloud-matrix].install_apk_url. The immutable timestamped per-build release (RSS notification) is separate and stays --latest=false.
gh_release._doc_publish_identity: 2026-10-06: the arm64 asset on 'latest' was the 2026-10-03 build while its .source sidecar carried the current identity (stamped at 13:37 by a run whose arm64 publish did not land), so the gate skipped every re-run and the fleet-setup contract (#873) never reached the arm64 APK. The gate hashes this directory, so this note is the source edit that moves the identity and republishes BOTH ABIs; a workflow_dispatch cannot (it carries no PUBLISH_GATE_FORCE and never stamps). If an asset is ever older than its sidecar again, that is the signal.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Encrypted Matrix messaging for the fleet
about.description: Cloud Matrix is the fleet's Matrix client: end-to-end encrypted rooms, direct messages and spaces, and voice and video calls on the decentralised Matrix network, with the owner's homeserver as the default. It is a signed fork of Element X Android. It exists so secure group communication with people outside the fleet uses an open, federated protocol on the owner's own server.
features: Fleet updates and crash reports on the phone
guide: Sign in to the owner's homeserver.
Verify this session from another device to read encrypted history.
Start a call from the room's top bar.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.
about.credits: Upstream: Element X Android (github.com/element-hq/element-x-android) by New Vector Ltd, AGPL-3.0 or Element's commercial licence. The fleet build adds the fleet's update, crash and configs libraries.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
